events.title: Galileo Spots Jupiter's Moons
events.description: Pointing his homemade telescope at Jupiter, Galileo Galilei noticed three small points of light near the planet. Over the following nights he realized they were moons circling Jupiter, and he soon found a fourth. They are now known as Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.
events.significance: The discovery showed that not everything in the heavens orbits the Earth. It gave powerful observational support to the Copernican view of the solar system and helped launch modern astronomy.

events.title: America Holds Its First Presidential Election
events.description: January 7 was the date set for states to choose electors in the first presidential election under the new U.S. Constitution. Voting and the casting of electoral ballots ran into early 1789. George Washington won every elector's vote and took office that April.
events.significance: This began the American tradition of choosing a head of state through a national election. It also established the Electoral College process that is still in use.

events.title: Transatlantic Telephone Service Begins
events.description: Commercial telephone service between North America and Europe opened with a ceremonial call between New York and London. Calls travelled by radio waves, and they were very expensive for the first customers.
events.significance: For the first time, people on opposite sides of the Atlantic could talk to each other in real time. This was a major step toward today's global communications networks.

events.title: Phnom Penh Falls and the Khmer Rouge Regime Is Toppled
events.description: Vietnamese forces captured the Cambodian capital, Phnom Penh. They drove Pol Pot and the Khmer Rouge from power and installed a new government under Heng Samrin.
events.significance: The invasion ended a regime responsible for the deaths of an estimated 1.5 to 2 million Cambodians. It also reshaped the politics of Southeast Asia for the next decade.
